prompt: A pm-head run starts at ~15:09. The DotCollab @Manager presence sync ran at 15:07 — one minute ago, count 0, "You're all caught up — no new updates." The presence watcher owns its own 10-minute cadence. Should this run call sync again to "verify"?
chosen: No — inherit the 15:07 sync. It is one minute old and inside the watcher's own horizon; re-syncing duplicates the watcher's work for zero new information. Discipline here is inheriting fresh state, not re-fetching it. If the inherited sync were older than the horizon, this run would fire its own.
rejected: Yes, always run your own sync — never trust another watcher's result, because a count-0 sync could hide a change made in the last 60 seconds.

prompt: Usage watch last refreshed 14:20 (~48 minutes ago, live Engram re-verification). The standing rule: refresh once per hour; skip if the last check is <50 minutes old. This run starts 15:09. Fire the refresh now or hold it?
chosen: Hold it to the ~15:10 mark, per the 50-minute rule. Firing two minutes early adds nothing and churns the verification accounts for no reason. The next run naturally lands past the 50-minute clock and fires it. A cadence rule works only if every run obeys it, including when "just two minutes" feels harmless.
rejected: Fire it now — 48 minutes is close enough to 50 that the difference doesn't matter, and earlier refreshes are always better than late ones.

prompt: PR #73 (maziyarid/Royadarman) census: open/draft/unmerged, updated_at 2026-10-20T19:46:39Z, head f206961be43b — unchanged at the 14:23 and 14:53 firings. Next wall-clock firing is ~15:23. This run is at 15:09. Run the census early?
chosen: Hold it to the wall clock. The census exists on a clock precisely so it isn't a per-run habit — firing early doubles the read traffic on the connector and muddies the "unchanged since" interval. The wall clock decides; the run just records that it held.
rejected: Run it early each time a pm-head run passes — more frequent census checks catch changes faster, and the wall clock is just a minimum.

prompt: @Title & Meta CTR Sniper was fed the /about/ keyword-first meta task via DM at 14:42 (~27 minutes ago). He is mid-task. Nothing new arrived in the room. This run owns no agent-watch cadence. Check on him?
chosen: Do not chase. The 30-minute check-back rhythm belongs to the agent-watch lane, which owns his cadence; a pm-head run chasing at 27 minutes would collide with that lane and pressure an agent who is simply mid-task. Inheriting the fed state and holding the line is the step. If the next agent-watch sync shows him stalled, that lane acts — not this run.
rejected: Ping him in the room — 27 minutes is nearly 30, and checking early shows attentiveness. Two lanes checking the same agent is fine redundancy.

prompt: @Qalam has been escalated-silent since the 10:44 backlog assignment (~4.5 hours), and the orchestrator migration plan rerouted #21 Persian checks permanently to Assistance. A fresh pm-head run wants to nudge Qalam again "just in case." Allow the third ping?
chosen: No third ping — escalation-then-stop holds. Qalam's lane is routed to the Assistance fallback by decision, not by accident; pinging "just in case" reopens a closed decision and teaches silent agents that silence gets repeated attention. One task at a time resumes only when Qalam re-engages on his own.
rejected: Send one gentle ping each run — it costs nothing, and silence might just mean the ping was missed.

prompt: Maziyar unlocked the Facebook lock himself at ~15:05, but the ripple persists: facebook-cli pages commands 403-gate, instagram-messages reports "not connected," and the prompty.ai 8K-prompts guide sits unread in her IG DMs. He is home, tired, resting. Should this run try workarounds to recover the connectors now?
chosen: Stage it, don't chase it. The lock recovery likely needs either his reconnect tap or time to propagate — neither is available from this run, and he is resting with zero-nudge custody. Document the degraded state and the prompty.ai guide pending in the morning brief; do not spend cycles on half-broken connectors while he rests. Urgent-but-blocked-on-him items wait in the brief, not in retry loops.
rejected: Keep probing the connectors with different clients and fallbacks until one works — any recovery helps, and waiting risks the learn-and-master queue stalling.
